attrs.evidence: FOUR occurrences of one class, and the fourth landed in the round that shipped this claim. The R4 brief said `60 records` over a 62-record ledger; the R7.2 brief said `21 sustained defeaters` where the gate printed 22; INV-R8.3 said `four files ship` over six declared untrusted captures; and INV-R9 typed `PROVED 15, OPEN 7, DECLARED 6, KNOWN 3, PROVISIONAL 2, REFUTED 2` into FAC-INTEGRATION-READJUDICATE while describing 34 imports — a histogram that sums to 35, because the fifteenth PROVED candidate is the one disposed as already_present. THE MECHANISM IS THREE PARTS AND THEIR SCOPE IS NOW STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. (a) mosaic/derived/brief-facts.json is DERIVED by check-mosaic §13 and the bundle substitutes {{KEY}} from it, refusing a bare integer before a declared noun in a source brief — this covers BRIEFS and the keys someone thought to derive. (b) check-mosaic §7 matches counted phrases in the ledger’s prose — a backstop over a fixed phrase list. (c) INV-R9.2 adds derivation at the point of use for two more surfaces: check-integration §histogram computes every status histogram from the bucket records and refuses one typed into an integration claim’s prose, and check-lineage §8 derives transition scope and refuses a receipt stating its own. NOTHING COVERS PROSE IN GENERAL.
attrs.gap: THE CLAIM AS ORIGINALLY WORDED — `no count of a registry-derivable quantity is typed into prose` — IS FALSIFIED BY ITS OWN ROUND and is not what the mechanism enforces. What is enforced is: brief text through substitution; the ledger prose a fixed phrase list reaches; integration status histograms; receipt transition scope. A count phrased outside those four surfaces passes, and the R9 histogram is the proof — it was in a ledger field, and §7’s phrase list did not contain that shape, because a phrase list contains the drifts someone has already thought of. THE HONEST FORM OF THE RULE IS NEGATIVE — prose should not state a derivable count at all — and deciding whether a sentence states a cardinality is the definitional-subsumption problem this ledger declined to mechanise at INV-R6. A HISTORICAL count must also stay a literal (`R7.1 counted 21 repaired defects` is a fact about a past state), so the lint carries an as-of form, and every count in this evidence field about a PAST artifact is one of those.
attrs.implementation_binding: scripts/check-mosaic.mjs — P.ledgerProseCounts (§7) and the §13 brief-facts derivation
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's adjudication of the Fable R8.3 pass, §9: adopt the rule, not the regex implementation — prefer structured fields and generated sentences; a heuristic prose checker may be a backstop, not the source of truth. The two mechanisms this claim names were built on the R7.x lane and arrived here through the INV-R9 content integration.
attrs.review_focus: The claim is about an ORDERING between two mechanisms, not about either one. Is `structured field first, phrase match second` actually what the code does, or does the phrase list still carry weight the structured half should? And: the R8.3 drift was found by an outside reader on a shipped artifact, not by either mechanism — is there a class of count that neither half can reach in principle?
attrs.statement: No count of a registry-derivable quantity is typed into prose ON A SURFACE THIS MECHANISM COVERS: brief text, ledger prose the phrase list reaches, integration status histograms, and receipt transition scope. The quantity is computed where it is printed, or stated as a derived key the build substitutes; a phrase-matching check over prose is a backstop and never the source of truth.
